## Project overview

**metafi-nextjs-shadcnblocks** is a Next.js 15 template with Contentful, shadcn/ui, and Tailwind 4. It uses a BlockRenderer pattern to render CMS-driven sections (Hero, FAQ, TabbedContent, Features, DataViz, etc.) with live preview.

## Cursor setup

### Agents

- **`add-contentful-block`** (`.cursor/agents/add-contentful-block.md`) – Orchestrates adding new Contentful blocks:
  - Phase 0: Discovery (contentful-block-discovery)
  - Phase 1: Q&A
  - Phase 2: Content model proposal
  - Phase 2.5: Entry preview
  - Phase 3: Implementation (M1–M5)
  - Mandatory STOP points for user approval
  - Test gates at each milestone

### Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `contentful-block-discovery` | Phase 0 discovery for new blocks |
| `contentful-block-graphql-types` | M1: GraphQL fragments, queries, mappers |
| `contentful-block-component` | M2: React component + block config |
| `contentful-mcp-create-model` | M3: Content types and entries via MCP |
| `contentful-block-live-preview` | M4: ID-based live preview |
| `contentful-live-preview-verify` | M5: Verify live preview in browser |
| `continuous-improvement` | Post-run: archive tasks, update lessons-learned |

### Rules

- **bun-package-manager.mdc** – Use Bun for all package operations  
- **contentful-live-preview-debug.mdc** – Context for Contentful preview debugging (parent vs iframe, data flow)  
- **oscar-prompting.mdc** (user rule) – OSCAR framework for debugging prompts

## Recommendation: keep README lean, link to docs

### 1. Avoid a single large README

- README should stay short and focused on first-run experience.
- Long READMEs are hard to maintain and navigate.
- You already have a `documentation/` structure; use it.

### 2. Use README as a hub

Keep README as the entry point and add a short “Documentation” section that links out:

```
## Documentation

- [Codebase Architecture](documentation/CODEBASE-ARCHITECTURE.md) — Project structure, tech stack, routes
- [Component Reference](documentation/COMPONENT-REFERENCE.md) — Layout and section components
- [Development Guide](documentation/DEVELOPMENT-GUIDE.md) — Adding pages, sections, blog posts
- [Component Live Preview](documentation/component-live-preview.md) — ID-based preview for Contentful blocks
- [Lessons Learned](documentation/lessons-learned.md) — Error patterns and fixes (for debugging)
```

### 3. Update Contentful section

Add a concise block list and link to the live preview doc:

```
Content types: Page, Hero, FAQ, TabbedContent, Features, DataViz. See component-live-preview.md for adding new blocks.
```

### 4. Optional: Cursor / agent section

If you want agents and contributors to know about the workflow:

```
## Cursor / Agent Setup

- **add-contentful-block** agent: Orchestrates adding new Contentful blocks (discovery → content model → implementation).
- **Skills**: contentful-block-discovery, contentful-block-graphql-types, contentful-block-component, etc.
- See `.cursor/agents/add-contentful-block.md` for the full workflow.
```

### 5. What to keep in README vs docs

| In README | In documentation/ |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Getting started (install, run) | Architecture, structure |
| Tech stack (short) | Component reference |
| Contentful setup (env vars, app URL) | Dev guide (adding pages, sections) |
| Block list (one line) | Content model proposal |
| Links to key docs | Lessons learned |
| Deploy instructions | Migration plan |
